explanation: A biblical figure, later called Abraham, who is an important patriarch in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
Abraham's nephew who lived in Sodom and was taken captive during the war between the kings.
King of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abram after his victory over the kings.
The king of Elam who led a coalition of kings against Sodom and Gomorrah and took Lot captive.
An ancient city, identified with Jerusalem, where Melchizedek was both king and priest.
One of the two biblical cities, along with Sodom, that were destroyed by God because of their wickedness and sin.
An agreement or pact between two or more parties, often to cooperate toward a common goal or protect one another.
A person held in captivity, often as a result of war or conflict.
Success in battle or competition, often used in connection with war or military campaigns.
A tax or levy, usually one-tenth of income or property, given to God or a priest as an expression of gratitude and reverence.
